content.text:
The evidence points consistently to a real physical change rather than a sensor fault:

- The Core_mid (F3_Z01) temperature genuinely rose after July 2018 (monthly mean ~23.5°C before → ~25.1°C after), while the reference zone F2_Z02 stayed flat (~24.6°C).
- The reading still varies normally (570 distinct values), stays in a plausible range (20.3–27.1°C), and tracks healthy zones tightly (hourly correlation rises to ~0.9) — i.e., not a stuck/frozen or implausible value, which is the usual fault signature.
- The zone's VAV damper setpoint increased in response (quarterly mean 0.18 in Q1 → 0.44 in Q3), showing the control loop reacting to a real temperature rise, consistent with higher cooling demand from increased internal/core load.

Data support: **local load change**.
